THE FULL BREAKDOWN

A deposit is the total.
We’ll show the detail.

Amazon combines sales with refunds, marketplace fees, adjustments and reserve movements. The planned settlement view brings those components together so you can see how the payout was calculated.

Review the accounting categories before posting. Your Xero records should explain the activity, not just repeat the deposit amount.

BUILT AROUND REVIEW

From settlement to Xero.

Account and tax mappings depend on your business. The intended workflow keeps those decisions visible.

  1. 01

    Import

    Bring in available settlement data from your authorised Amazon account.

  2. 02

    Map

    Assign sales, fees, refunds and other categories to the appropriate Xero accounts.

  3. 03

    Review & post

    Check the breakdown and resolve missing information before sending entries.

  4. 04

    Match

    Use the prepared entries to match the corresponding bank deposit in Xero.

BEYOND THE HAPPY PATH

When something needs attention,
you should know why.

Data readiness

Waiting on a report?

We plan to distinguish missing reports and tax data from entries that are ready to review, so you can understand the next step.

Reporting periods

Two months. One payout.

Month-end activity and bank payout dates can differ. Period-aware reporting is part of the planned reconciliation scope.

Cash movements

Held doesn’t mean lost.

Reserve movements affect cash available for payout. They need to be visible separately from the sales and costs behind profitability.

A precise promise.

Reconcile Ready is in development. We plan to help prepare and review accounting entries; final bank matching happens in Xero. Regional tax support, multi-currency handling and automatic posting options will be confirmed before launch.
